title: PR #482 — notification fan-out
summary: Replaces the inline email send with a strategy-per-channel dispatcher behind a factory, and emits a domain event so the audit log stays decoupled.

surface.name: NotificationChannel
surface.note: The interface a new channel implements. Additive, so nothing outside the module has to change.

surface.name: ChannelName
surface.note: A union of 'email' and 'sms'. Widening it later is a one-line change here plus a case in the switch.

surface.name: POST /notifications
surface.note: The body now needs a channel field. An existing client that omits it gets an UnsupportedChannelError, which the controller maps to a 502 rather than a 400.

surface.name: mail.sent
surface.note: Renamed to notification.sent. Any listener outside this repo bound to mail.sent goes quiet with no error.

surface.name: notification.sent
surface.note: Carries channel and to. The audit row now records the channel instead of assuming mail.

surface.name: TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
surface.note: TwilioClient reads it at construction, so a deploy without it fails at boot rather than at the first SMS.

reading_order.why: Fifteen lines, and every other file in the diff is shaped by them. Read the interface and the ChannelName union first and the rest follows.
The new middle. It holds the channel registry, the switch, and the emit, so it is where the refactor's decisions live.
What was taken out. Compare the 21 deleted lines against the dispatcher you just read: this is the same behaviour, one layer down.
The moved code, unchanged in substance. Skim it to confirm nothing was lost in the move.
The new capability, and the only untested file. This is where to spend review time: it drops payload.template and needs an env var nothing else needs.
The blast radius. A different team owns this file and the event it listens for was renamed, so read it last but do not skip it.

risks.statement: An SMS gets the subject line and nothing else. SmsChannel drops payload.template, so any notification with a body renders as its subject over SMS.
risks.question: Is a subject-only SMS the intended message, or should the template render for SMS too?

risks.statement: A client that omits the new channel field gets an UnsupportedChannelError, which the controller maps to a 502 rather than a 400. A caller's bad request reads as our outage.
risks.question: Should an unknown channel be a 400, and should channel default to email for existing clients?

risks.statement: The audit kind column now holds the channel name instead of the constant 'mail', so rows written before and after this deploy mean different things with no marker between them.
risks.question: Does anything query audit rows by kind = 'mail'?

risks.statement: A failed channel throws and nothing retries. The old inline mailer call had the same behaviour, so this is not a regression, but the dispatcher is now the obvious place for a retry and does not have one.
risks.question: Is a dropped notification acceptable, or does this need a retry before it ships?

risks.statement: TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN is read when TwilioClient is constructed, so a deploy missing it fails at boot rather than at the first SMS. Loud is better than silent here, but it needs to be in the deploy config before this merges.
risks.question: Is the token already in every environment's config?

nodes.label: notification.controller.ts
nodes.summary: The HTTP entry point. It used to build the email body and call MailerService itself; now it validates the request and hands the payload to the dispatcher, so the controller no longer knows which channels exist.
details: 21 removed lines are the inline template building, now gone from the controller.
Dispatcher arrives by constructor injection at line 29.

tests.note: The existing spec asserts a 201 and mocks the dispatcher, so it passes either way. Nothing asserts the template building is gone.

history.note: Six authors in three months, and every notification feature lands here first. That is the reason for the refactor, and the reason to read this file's diff twice.

hunks.explanation: The controller stops knowing how a notification is delivered. Template rendering and the MailerService call are gone; both now live behind the dispatcher, and the constructor takes the dispatcher instead of the mailer.

nodes.label: dispatcher.service.ts
nodes.summary: New file. Holds the channel registry, resolves one channel per request from the notification payload, runs it, then emits notification.sent so nothing downstream has to be called inline.
details: channelFor() at line 92 maps the channel name to a concrete strategy with a switch.
Emits notification.sent at line 71 after a successful send, inside the same try block.
No retry here: a failed channel throws and the controller maps it to a 502.

tests.note: Covers both channels and the unsupported-channel throw. The notification.sent emit is asserted at line 64.

history.note: New file, so no history. It inherits the controller's traffic: the next channel change lands here instead.

hunks.explanation: The whole delivery path in one method: pick a channel, send, announce it. The catch logs and rethrows rather than swallowing, so a dead channel still surfaces as a 502 at the controller.
The one place that knows the channel names. Adding a third channel means one case here and one new class, which is the trade the refactor was after.
The code deleted from the controller, moved here behind the interface. MailerService is untouched: only the caller changed.
The new capability the refactor was for. It drops payload.template entirely, so an SMS gets the subject line and nothing else - worth a question in review.

tests.note: New file, no spec. The Twilio call and the dropped template are both unasserted, which is the gap worth arguing about in this diff.

hunks.explanation: Four lines that hold the refactor together. ChannelName is the union the switch is checked against, so a new channel that skips this file fails to compile.

tests.note: Types only. The compiler is the test.

nodes.label: audit.listener.ts
nodes.summary: Rewritten to react to notification.sent instead of being called by the send path. Same audit rows written, but the write is no longer on the request's critical path.

hunks.explanation: The listener follows the renamed event. The audit row now records which channel was used instead of assuming mail, so old rows and new rows carry different meaning in the kind column.

tests.note: The renamed event is covered. No case asserts what happens to rows written under the old mail.sent name.

history.note: Quiet file, and owned by a different team than the rest of the diff. The event rename needs their eyes.

nodes.label: mailer.service.ts
nodes.summary: Untouched; now called only from the email channel.
details: Untouched by this PR; only its caller changed.

nodes.label: NotificationDispatcher
nodes.summary: Holds the channel registry and resolves one per request.
details: channelFor holds the concrete channels, returning this.email or this.sms per case, so adding a third means editing this switch.
Everything downstream of that switch is typed as NotificationChannel, so dispatch itself never names a channel.

patterns.name: Strategy
patterns.intent: One interface per delivery channel so the dispatcher does not branch on channel type.

evidence.explanation: One method, one return type, no channel name anywhere in the signature. That is what lets the dispatcher stop knowing which provider it is talking to.
The three-branch if is gone. The dispatcher now asks for an implementation and calls it, so adding a fourth channel never touches this method.

patterns.name: Factory Method
patterns.intent: channelFor() maps a channel name to a concrete strategy.

evidence.explanation: The switch moved here and returns injected instances, not new ones. It picks a product and hands it back, which is the whole of Factory Method.

patterns.note: Medium: it is a plain switch, not a registry, so adding a channel still edits this function.

patterns.name: Observer
patterns.intent: Audit log reacts to a domain event instead of being called inline.

evidence.explanation: The dispatcher emits after the channel returns. It names an event and a payload, never a listener, so audit can be added or dropped without editing this method. That is the Subject half of the pair.
The Observer half. It subscribes by event name, which is what makes this Observer and not a direct call. The rename from mail.sent is the same edit the contract surface lists as breaking.
